clue.text: Woman priest, one who runs things

blocks.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A female cleric presented as the person in charge of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is a manager who heads an organisation or production.

clue.text: Sort of currency claimed when travelling

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of the word before it move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of money that a traveller says they hold, as on an expense claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimal currency is divided into units of ten or a hundred, as Britain's was from 1971.

clue.text: Unstable, like some mountain peaks?

blocks.note: first meaning: wobbly or shaky
second meaning: stony, and also a nod to the ... Mountains of North America

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second meaning, which hints at a named mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means shaky or insecure, and also full of rocks, as are the summits of the North American range.

clue.text: Support son over joint sports contest, perhaps

blocks.note: to champion a cause is to support it
S is the abbreviation for son
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Backing a boy with a bad hip in a sporting tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the son above the joint, so S comes before HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A championship is a competition to decide the champion, of which a sporting tournament is one example.

clue.text: It hurts to give licence to young bird

blocks.note: ow is the cry of someone in pain
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A painful business, granting a permit to a fledgling.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a baby owl, a juvenile bird.

clue.text: Prophet a doctor originally supported

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the next word, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
first letter of supported

explanation.surface: A prophet who was backed by a physician from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Decree DA meant to develop

indicators.note: to develop means to grow into something different, so the letters reshape into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An order that a District Attorney intended to evolve.
explanation.walkthrough: A DA is a District Attorney, the public prosecutor in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or command, a decree.

clue.text: Grasslike plant primarily straggling border

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: first letter of straggling
an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: A grassy plant spreading untidily along the edge of a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant with triangular stems that grows in wet ground.

clue.text: Painter does what would-be MP may hope to do

definitions.text: does what would-be MP may hope to do
definitions.note: a verb phrase defining the split form GAINS BOROUGH

blocks.note: first meaning: Thomas ..., the 18th-century English portrait and landscape painter

blocks.clueFragment: does what would-be MP may hope to do
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: a parliamentary candidate hopes to win a constituency

explanation.walkthrough: A borough was a type of parliamentary constituency, so a candidate hopes to win (gain) one; read as two words the painter's name says exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsborough was a leading English artist, famed for portraits such as The Blue Boy.

clue.text: Drink provided by commander in short outdoor garment

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the garment word loses its final letter
in places one element inside the other one

blocks.note: a coat is worn outside
CO is Commanding Officer

explanation.surface: A hot drink served by an officer wearing a cropped coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a description of the garment's style, but it means cutting the word's last letter before the commander goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans and milk.

clue.text: Erudite Shakespearean king with extremely nubile daughters

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: King Lear, the tragedy's title character
outer letters of nubile
D is the abbreviation for daughter(s)

explanation.surface: A king from Shakespeare whose daughters are of marriageable age, which fits Lear and his three daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) and erudite both describe someone with deep scholarly knowledge.

clue.text: Hawthorn blossom could — possibly

blocks.note: first meaning: the flower of the hawthorn tree
second meaning: the modal verb of possibility

explanation.surface: A tentative suggestion about whether the hawthorn might flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names hawthorn flowers, which open in May, and the verb expresses something that might possibly happen.

clue.text: Overlord's shelter by river at end of estate

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the first letter of 'estate'

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a tent is a canvas shelter
taken as written
last letter of estate

explanation.surface: A lord's hut beside a river at the far edge of his land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places the shelter next to the river, with the river coming first; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler with great power, an overlord.

clue.text: Drink to follow for small pet

blocks.note: to lap is to drink as a cat or dog does
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: An instruction to have a drink and then follow, apparently for a pet's sake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered dog kept as a companion.

clue.text: In favour of light weight computer file

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Backing a small digital document, like a light file.
explanation.walkthrough: PROGRAM is the spelling used for computing even in Britain, where 'programme' is used otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A program is a set of coded instructions stored as an executable file that a computer runs.

clue.text: Aim to express disapproval

blocks.note: first meaning: a goal or purpose
second meaning: to protest

explanation.surface: Setting out with the intention of voicing a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a purpose; as a verb, stressed on the second syllable, it means to protest.

clue.text: Doctor drank a pint at last — from this?

definitions.text: Doctor drank a pint at last — from this?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the following letters are rearranged
at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of pint

explanation.surface: Wondering which vessel a beer was finally drunk out of.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a pint is drunk from this, so the entire clue is the definition as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, often pewter, from which a pint is drunk.

clue.text: Angry about a hybrid style of music

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
over means concerning, as in 'a row over money'

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by a musical genre that mixes styles.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossover music blends genres, such as classical pieces given a pop treatment.

clue.text: Sturdy horse runs over a venomous snake

blocks.note: a cob is a stocky short-legged horse
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strong horse bolting past a poisonous reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts COB above R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a poisonous snake that raises a hood when threatened.

clue.text: Sign right in the centre of Galician port

indicators.note: in the centre of places one element in the middle of the place name that follows

blocks.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, north-west Spain
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A signpost directly in the middle of a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo, the Virgin, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Family member, one that shines, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word comes from hearing it said, not from seeing it written

blocks.note: the sun shines in the sky

explanation.surface: A relative described as a shining light, according to what we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, a member of the family.

clue.text: Relax on a rug initially, playing this instrument?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: to sit is to rest
taken as written
first letter of rug

explanation.surface: Lounging on a carpet while strumming an instrument, as a sitar player traditionally does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts SIT above A R; the scene also fits, as the sitar is played seated on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian lute, an instrument played sitting cross-legged.

clue.text: Scottish writer given right to build obstacle

blocks.note: J M Barrie, the Scottish author of Peter Pan
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Scottish author granted permission to construct a blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is a fence or obstruction that prevents passage, an obstacle.

clue.text: Extremist involved in adult radicalisation

indicators.note: involved in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning them

blocks.note: the letters run across the word break

explanation.surface: A militant who played a part in turning grown-ups to radical views.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, especially in politics.

clue.text: Leader leaving crazy military force

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and its leaving means it is dropped from the word

blocks.note: barmy is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A commander quitting an insane fighting unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is everyday British slang for crazy or foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of soldiers, a land-based fighting force.

clue.text: Troubled bloke crossing the river Wye at last

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across something, so the man's word straddles the other letters
at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: bod is informal British for a person or chap
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
last letter of Wye

explanation.surface: A worried man fording the River Wye at the end of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wye is a river on the England–Wales border, but here it only supplies its final letter; 'river' is the abbreviation instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered means worried or disturbed, the same as troubled.
